code.description:
The problem code of its error (`SH1002`), or of its failure when
it ran and failed on the setup (`doctor`); `shuyi explain <code>`
prints its page.

error.description: Why it could not run, if it could not.

help.description: How to fix it, with the code.

limits.description: What it could not determine, in plain words.

ok.description:
Whether it passed: nothing found by a check, runs that agree, a
game made, a toolchain complete. False too when it could not run.

result.description: What it found or made; absent when it could not run.

FrameRecord.description: What one frame measured. Build it with [`FrameRecord::new`] (ADR-0039).

heap.description:
The heap's counts at the frame's end, where the backend counts it
(a debug build of `shuyi-app` or a tool program); `None` where it
doesn't, and left out of the JSON then.

spans.description:
The spans that ended in it, in the order they ended (an inner one
before its outer one), at most [`MAX_SPANS`].

spans_dropped.description: The spans past [`MAX_SPANS`], counted and not kept.

FrameTimes.description:
How long the parts of one frame took, in whole microseconds. Build it
with [`FrameTimes::new`] (ADR-0039); a backend may add a part.

draw_us.description:
The drawing: the screens and the modules drawing the frame
([`Game::redraw`](crate::Game::redraw)).

frame_us.description:
[`present_us`](Self::present_us) plus this frame from its start to
its end: never less than the four above together. The rest is
`App`'s own (the system's events, the audio, the record).

paint_us.description:
The platform's `present`: in `shuyi-app`, painting the frame into
the window.

present_us.description:
From the end of the last frame to the start of this one, outside
`App`: the backend's buffer swap and its wait for vsync or the frame
cap. 0 on the first frame measured.

update_us.description:
`Game::frame` from its start to the drawing: the input, the
modules' `before_update` and the screens' update.

HeapCounts.description:
The heap's counts at a frame's end, in bytes asked for (never the
allocator's own overhead). Build it with [`HeapCounts::new`]
(ADR-0039).

allocs.description:
The calls that allocated or reallocated since the last reading: one
reading a frame, so the frame's.

live_bytes.description: The bytes allocated and not yet freed.

peak_bytes.description: The most bytes live at once since the program started.

HeapDiff.description:
What grew and shrank in the heap between two snapshots
([`HeapSnapshot::diff`]). Build an empty one with [`HeapDiff::new`]
(ADR-0039).

live_bytes.description: How many more bytes are live: less than 0 for fewer.

tags.description:
The tags whose live bytes or blocks changed: the largest change in
bytes first (more or fewer), then by class, then by name.

HeapSnapshot.description:
What holds the heap at a frame (ADR-0046 §6): its live bytes, and each
memory tag's counts. Build it with [`HeapSnapshot::new`] (ADR-0039),
which puts the rows in order; compare two with [`diff`](Self::diff).

frame.description:
The frame it was taken after (frames count from 1; 0 is before the
first).

live_bytes.description: The bytes allocated and not yet freed.

overflowed.description:
How many names had no tag of their own, past the counter's table,
and count under `overflow`.

peak_bytes.description: The most bytes live at once since the program started.

tags.description:
Each tag with bytes live or ever allocated under it: the most live
bytes first, then by class, then by name.

HeapSummary.description: How the heap's counts add up over a trace's records, in bytes asked for.

allocs.description: How the allocations per frame spread.

live_bytes.description: The bytes live at the last record's end.

peak_bytes.description: The most bytes live at once, the most of the records' peaks.

oneOf.description: A new game from a template.
Every error of the game's content.
What is wrong with the shape of the game's code.
The catalog of modules, and the game's.
A module turned on.
A key script played headless.
The scene on screen.
A record replayed.
Bots playing the game.
Named bots' tries judged against the game's checks.
A stage changed until the game's named bots land in their bands.
A file read through the format registry.
The game's sources baked into a pack.
The toolchain checked.
A problem code's page.
A running build reached over the live link.
The MCP session's game started headless.
The MCP session's game played on: a script, then idle frames.
A picture of the MCP session's frame.
What happened in the MCP session's game.
The MCP session's frames' records since a number.
The MCP session's game started again.
The MCP session's game stopped.

PerfOutput.description: What `perf` read of the session's frames.

diff.description: What changed from the snapshot of `diff_from`, with it.

dropped.description: How many records numbered `since` or more were no longer kept.

kept.description:
The frames of the snapshots the session keeps, oldest first: the
`diff_from` it takes.

next.description: The number to pass as `since` next time.

records.description: The frames' records numbered `since` or more, oldest first.

snapshot.description:
The heap snapshot taken now, with `snapshot`: null without it, or
where the heap isn't counted by tag.

summary.description: What the records answered add up to; none when there are none.

PerfSummary.description: What a trace's records add up to.

dropped.description: How many earlier frames' records were no longer kept.

file.description: The trace file written, its absolute path, with `--perf-out`.

frame.description: How the whole frame's time spread (`frame_us`).

frames.description: The records summed up: the frames kept.

heap.description:
The heap's counts over the records that have them; null where none
has (a release build of the tool program, or one opted out).

heap_growth.description:
What grew and shrank from the snapshot before the run to the one
after: the diff, with its first ten rows, the largest change first.
Null without snapshots.

heap_tags.description:
What held the heap after the last frame: the snapshot's first ten
rows by tag, the most live bytes first. Empty without a snapshot.

paint.description: How painting into the window spread (`paint_us`).

present.description: How the backend's swap and wait spread (`present_us`).

spans.description:
The spans with the most time in all, most first (ties by name), at
most five.

SpanEvent.description: A span a game marked ([`Ctx::span`](crate::Ctx::span)), as it ended.

depth.description: How many spans it was inside: 0 for one inside no other.

start_us.description: When it started, in microseconds from the frame's start.

us.description: How long it took, in microseconds.

SpanSummary.description: A span's name and how its time adds up over the records.

mean_us.description: Its mean time, in microseconds, rounded down.

total_us.description: Its time in all, in microseconds.

Spread.description:
How a set of times spread, in whole microseconds: the median, the 99th
percentile (nearest rank), the worst and the mean rounded down.

p50.description: The median: half the times are this or less.

p99.description: 99 in a hundred times are this or less.

TagClass.description:
What a memory tag names (ADR-0046 §6): the heap counter counts each
block under the innermost tag entered when it was allocated. Its number
is the class a backend's counter keeps with each name
([`MemoryScopes::tag`]); `Other` is 0, the class of the counter's own
`other` and `overflow`.

oneOf.description:
A phase of the frame: `load`, `update`, `draw`, `paint`, `perf`,
and `app` for the rest of `App`'s frame.
A span the game marked ([`Ctx::span`](crate::Ctx::span)).
An asset kind being decoded: `image`, `palette`, …

None of those: `other`, what is allocated outside any tag, and
`overflow`, the names past the counter's table.

TagDelta.description:
How one memory tag changed between two snapshots. Build it with
[`TagDelta::new`] (ADR-0039).

live_blocks.description: How many more blocks are live under it: less than 0 for fewer.

live_bytes.description: How many more bytes are live under it: less than 0 for fewer.

TagRow.description:
One memory tag's counts in a [`HeapSnapshot`], in bytes asked for.
Build it with [`TagRow::new`] (ADR-0039).

allocated_bytes.description: The bytes ever allocated under it: a block grown adds its new size.

class.description: What the tag names: a phase, a span, an asset kind, or `other`.

live_bytes.description:
The bytes live under it: allocated, or last grown, under it and not
yet freed.

name.description:
Its name: `update`, the span's (`ai`), the asset kind's (`image`),
`other` or `overflow`.

peak_bytes.description: The most bytes live under it at once.
